# Audit — wayfinder (read-understand-gap) · @ ed37663 · 2026-07-28

**What:** The heaviest orchestrator: plans work too big for one session as a MAP issue (label wayfinder:map) + child DECISION tickets on the tracker. Concepts: destination (named first, fixes scope), map-as-index (decisions live in tickets, map only gists+links), ticket types research(AFK)/prototype(HITL)/grilling(HITL)/task, claims via assignee, blocking via native tracker edges, frontier = open+unblocked+unclaimed, fog of war ("Not yet specified" = in-scope but not yet sharp; test = can you STATE the question, not answer it), out-of-scope section (never graduates). Two modes: chart (grill destination → breadth-first frontier → create map+tickets → wire blocking second pass → fire research subagents → stop) and work (load map → claim ONE ticket → resolve → record → graduate fog). Hard rule: one ticket per session (research excepted). `disable-model-invocation: true`.
**Deps:** HEAVY — issue-tracker.md (setup) incl. its "Wayfinding operations" section; grilling, domain-modeling, research, prototype skills. Falls back to local-markdown tracker if none configured.
**Security:** clean — writes only tracker issues/files.
**Gaps/notes:** (1) Ticket sized "to one 100K token agent session" — with 1M windows this is conservative, but the smart-zone rationale (quality, not capacity) still holds; don't relitigate. (2) Fires parallel research subagents at chart time — the fan-out/graph-engineering candidate flagged in memory lives here natively; no extra tooling needed to trial it. (3) Hierarchy rule embodied: it invokes disciplines (grilling/research/prototype), never other orchestrators. ask-tete must hand wayfinder over as a command, never invoke it.
**Audit outcome:** clean; no complement material. Biggest infra consumer — verify tracker config before first use.
